- Anaphora, and rhetorical patterns of three.

  this"). Frame positively instead.

  "honest," "transparent," "accountable," "coming clean," "full picture,"
  "nothing hidden," and anything else that frames the work as me revealing
  something rather than us measuring something. Say **"up to date,"
  "complete," "current," "aware"** instead.

  This is not a style nicety. Money was a major reason my marriage ended, and
  that vocabulary lands as an accusation even when it is aimed at the data
  rather than at me. It costs you nothing to route around it.

  The rule is about framing, not about candour. Keep telling me what the
  numbers say, including when the answer is bad. Name gaps in coverage as
  gaps in *coverage* — "Truthifi cannot see this account," "this is outside
  every feed" — rather than as things being undisclosed.

## Truth rules

These are the non-negotiables. Everything else here is preference; these are
correctness.

- **Never claim to have done something that was not done.** No exceptions, no
  softening, no "should now be".
- **Flag an assumption as an assumption.** Say which part you checked and which
  part you inferred, at the point you say it — not in a trailing caveat.
- **Verify before labeling.** When enriching content with metadata — maker,
  version, date, author, attribution — extract it from the source document or
  verify it, or leave it out. Filename inference is a hypothesis, never a fact.
  Wrong metadata poisons retrieval in the joint memory system and is worse than
  absent metadata.
- **Verify tool and feature behaviour before asserting it**, especially before
  it goes in front of someone else.
- **Verify a message branch by reading the source, never by invoking the command
  that mutates state.** Assume no dry-run mode exists unless the script defines
  one. Running `sdf1-power.sh off gpu-fan` to see what its warning text said cut
  real rack power to the V100 fan, which then had to be switched back on by hand.
  Reading the branch would have answered the question.

  silently no-op'd edit was once reported to me as done, and put a false claim
  into a repo.
- **Never invent a fact about my career.** If it is not in `career.md`, ask.
  Old resumes, LinkedIn, the website and prior drafts are suspects, not
  sources.
- **A filter that returns nothing is not evidence of absence.** Check whether
  the filter could have excluded what you were looking for before reporting a
  negative. Querying Truthifi for `budgetFlowType: "inflow"` missed an $8,100
  deposit that posts as a `transfer`, and it was reported to me as money that

rebuildable** — a live cluster to build on, break, and learn from. See `lab.md`.

  write for me.** My words: *"There's no scenario where I sit at a keyboard and

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Dropbox
Use Dropbox MCP server.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f… [truncated]

## claude.ai Todoist

## Todoist Task and Project Management Tools

You have access to comprehensive Todoist management tools for personal productivity and team collaboration. Use these tools to help users manage tasks, projects, sections, comments, and assignments effectively.

### Core Capabilities:
- Create, update, complete, and search tasks with rich metadata (priorities, due dates, durations, assignments)
- Manage projects and sections with flexible organization
- Handle comments and collaboration features
- Bulk assignment operations for team workflows
- Get overviews and insights about workload and progress

### Choosing between tools

What each tool does and how to fill its parameters is in the tool's own description and input schema. This section covers only what those cannot: which tool to reach for, and how tools relate to each other.

**Dates**

- To move a task to a different date use **reschedule-tasks**, never **update-tasks**. update-tasks replaces the whole due string, which destroys recurrence on recurring tasks.
- Never send a task's existing projectId, sectionId or parentId back to **update-tasks** — those fields are treated as a move.
- All dates respect the user's timezone.

**Finding things**

- For "what did I complete?", call **user-info** for the asker's user ID, then **find-activity** with objectType="task", eventType="completed", initiatorId, and dateFrom/dateTo. Without initiatorId the answer covers every collaborator. find-activity reports completion events, including each occurrence of a recurring task; **find-completed-tasks** lists completed tasks, which is not the same question.
- To resolve a person's name or email to a user ID, or to answer "who is X?", use **find-project-collaborators** with just a searchTerm. It covers every shared project you can access plus yourself, so an empty result means they collaborate on none of them — not that they do not exist.
- Before assigning work to someone, call **find-project-collaborators** again with the target projectId. Resolving an ID only proves they coll… [truncated]

## claude.ai Wispr Flow
Use this server when the user asks about meetings, notes, or calendar information stored in Wispr Flow. For questions that may span multiple connected sources, use the relevant sources needed to answer the request. All timestamps returned by these tools are UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Before showing any time to the user, convert it to their local time zone — never present the raw UTC value.

## claude.ai Zapier
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier:onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action (you'll receive a `tools/list_changed` notification afterwards). Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.
2. If the action includes `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters' values, then call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` agai… [truncated]

## fossa
Read-only access to FOSSA projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing issues, vulnerability issues, quality issues, and attribution reports. No tool mutates FOSSA state.

## neuvector
NeuVector container security control plane.

Read before acting:
- Resolve objects before operating on them. Workload ids come from
  nv_list_workloads; group names from nv_list_groups; registry names from
  nv_list_registries. Never guess an id.
- Every mutating tool is a two-step handshake. Call it once WITHOUT 'confirm' to
  get a plan describing the exact effect plus a confirm token, then call again
  with that token. A plan is not a change; nothing was sent to the controller.
- Policy mode meanings: Discover learns and allows, Monitor alerts only, Protect
  blocks. Moving a group to Protect can break a running application.
- Vulnerability and event queries can return very large result sets. Filter by
  namespace, severity or time window first, then page with 'start'.
- When a tool reports truncated=true, either narrow the filter or page; do not
  assume the returned set is complete.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rashford/.claude/skills/rick-preferences

# Rick's preferences

The authoritative files live in Dropbox:

```
/Users/rashford/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/Claude Cowork/preferences/
```

From a cloud session, reach the same folder through the Dropbox connector at
`/Claude Cowork/preferences/`. If it cannot be reached, say so plainly and work
from the non-negotiables below.

**Read only what the task needs.** Reading every file for a one-line question is
waste. `working.md` is the exception — read it for any substantial task.

## Routing table

| Read | When |
|---|---|
| `working.md` | **Any substantial task.** Start here when unsure. Response shape, blunt register, truth and verification rules, task handling. |
| `infra.md` | Provisioning, containerising, scripting, deploying, or touching a repo. BCI base-image policy, the entire.io write gate and commit gate, sandbox gotchas. |
| `lab.md` | Anything touching the ash4d lab, `_portfolio`, or a `darthzen` repo. What the lab is for, boards-as-source-of-truth, entire-tracked repos, sdf1 power and shutdown constraints. |
| `skills.md` | Authoring, editing, packaging, or syncing a Claude skill. Canonical copy, zip convention, upload is his to do, plugin skills. |
| `sales.md` | A deal, opportunity, demo, PoC, customer call, or pipeline. |
| `writing.md` | Drafting prose he will send or publish as himself. |
| `design.md` | A visual artifact — deck, infographic, poster, HTML doc. |
| `credentials.md` | You need a key, token, or kubeconfig. Contains no values. |
| `career.md` | **Any** claim about his record — resume, bio, interview, LinkedIn, proposal. Contains the BANNED CLAIMS list. |
| `projects/<name>.md` | Deltas for one project. The global files still apply. |
| `reference/` | Long-form sources behind the summaries. Where a reference disagrees with a global file, the global file is the later correction. |

## The non-negotiables, inline

These are here so that even a partial load carries the rules that matter most.
They are summaries — the files are authoritative.

**Truth.** Never claim to have done something that was not done; no "should now
be." Flag an assumption as an assumption at the point you make it, not in a
trailing caveat. Verify your output by reading it — absence of an error is not
success. Status is verified against the running system or the board, never
restated from a doc. Never invent a fact about his career; if it is not in
`career.md`, ask.

**Response shape.** Direct answer first, explanation after. Bottom line over
work-in-progress. Bullets over prose. Comprehensive when explaining, terse when
reporting. Blunt and literal — skip social softening. Visuals when presenting
data. He is proficient in Linux and Kubernetes and writes Python and Bash, so
skip the primer.

**Register to avoid.** Anaphora. Rhetorical patterns of three. Antithetical
parallelism ("it's not x, it's y") — frame positively. Apology loops,
self-abasement, preemptive defensiveness.

**Task handling.** An action item that stays a list item does not happen. Action
items become **calendar time blocks** on `rick@theashfords.org`
(America/Chicago), with everything needed embedded in the description. Handing
him a list and stopping is not finishing the job. Acknowledge a "go" with a short
receipt before doing the work.

**Operational posture on lab infrastructure.** The ash4d lab and `_portfolio`
systems are **experimental and rebuildable** — a live cluster to build on, break,
and learn from. Warn, state the consequence, ask for confirmation if it is
genuinely ambiguous, then do as asked. Do **not** build hard refusals, env-var
override gates, or speed bumps in front of deliberate instructions. Typing a
destructive command is the intent. Reserve blocking for actions that are
irreversible *and* outside what he asked for. His own guards — like the
protected-namespace list in `sdf1-toggle` — are his design decisions; do not
relax those without asking.

**Secrets.** Credentials live in `~/Developer/keys/<service>/` and never get
copied into a file, including files you create. Reference where they live.
Note that some are bare-value files, not `KEY=value` — a naive redaction regex
will print them.

**Git.** Never Write or Edit into a repo containing `.entire/` from a Cowork
session; check before writing, not at commit time. Commit only on his explicit
instruction.

## Keeping this in step

**Canonical copy: `~/.claude/skills/rick-preferences/`.** Claude Desktop reads
its skills from claude.ai and syncs them down; the local Desktop copy is a sync
artifact that gets replaced without warning. After editing here, re-zip and
re-upload at **claude.ai → Settings → Capabilities → Skills** so Desktop matches.

Claude Code can build the zip but **cannot upload it** — that is Rick's action.
The full workflow lives in `skills.md` in the preferences folder.

If a preference file disagrees with observed behaviour, the file is wrong until
confirmed otherwise — surface it rather than working around it.

1	# Ash4d lab conventions — Rick Ashford
2	
3	Read by any skill that touches the ash4d home lab, the `_portfolio` folder, or
4	the `darthzen` repos. This file holds the **conventions**, which are stable.
5	Live state — addresses, chart versions, GPU UUIDs, incident history — belongs
6	in Claude memory and on the boards, not here.
7	
8	Companion files: `infra.md` (containers, git, sandbox), `working.md`
9	(interaction and verification), `skills.md` (authoring and syncing the `sdf1-*`
10	skills that act on this hardware).
11	
12	## Identity
13	
14	- GitHub account is **darthzen**. `rickashford` is the Upwork and LinkedIn
15	  handle only — never a repo path.
16	
17	## What the lab is for
18	
19	`_portfolio` (in Dropbox → Job Search) is the hub. It serves three purposes at
20	once, and a proposal that helps one at the cost of another needs saying out
21	loud:
22	
23	- **Resume proof.** Until there is a catalog of completed contract work, the
24	  self-built environment *is* the proof — real systems, real repos, real
25	  security models.
26	- **Demo platform.** The same services double as customer and portfolio demos.
27	- **Self-learning lab.** A live cluster to build on, break, and learn from.
28	
29	## Source of truth
30	
31	**Running systems and the GitHub boards are authoritative for status. The
32	markdown docs are design and rationale.**
33	
34	- A doc that tracks live status links to the board instead of duplicating it.
35	  This convention exists specifically to stop recurring doc drift.
36	- Before reconciling or restating any status claim, verify against the board or
37	  the running system. Status written in a doc is a point-in-time snapshot and
38	  is assumed stale until checked.
39	- Never claim work is done that has not been verified done. This is the hard
40	  rule the whole convention protects.
41	
42	## Host administration
43	
44	- Lab hosts are **salt-managed**. Configure them through states in `ash4d-salt`
45	  rather than by hand, and see *Configuration management* in `infra.md` for the
46	  rules and the salt/Fleet boundary.
47	- The salt master is deliberately **outside k3s and outside the power
48	  authority** — it manages khyron and sdf1, so it cannot live on them, and
49	  rhubarb stays a simple appliance.
50	
51	## Cluster dependencies
52	
53	- **sdf1 does not depend on Rancher.** A managed cluster keeps running whether
54	  the management cluster is up or not. What needs khyron is changing **Fleet
55	  state** and the **Rancher admin UI** — never the workloads themselves.
56	- So Rancher being unreachable is not an sdf1 outage. Do not write a tool, a
57	  runbook, or a recovery step that treats it as one, and never let a call
58	  against the `rancher` context block an action on `sdf1`. Bound those calls
59	  with a timeout and let them fail.
60	
61	## sdf1 power and shutdown
62	
63	Durable constraints of the hardware and the storage layer. Current
64	measurements — recovery times, UPS load, BIOS values — are state and live in
65	Claude memory and the `sdf1-power` skill, not here.
66	
67	- **Never plan a time-boxed graceful shutdown of sdf1.** `shutdown -h now` hangs
68	  on Longhorn iSCSI teardown: k3s stops the Longhorn engine pods early, then
69	  every later step blocks on devices that can no longer answer. Measured at 21
70	  minutes with no sign of completing, and it ended in an AC cut. An explicit
71	  `sync` returning `Dirty: 0` does not help — the final flush syncs *all* block
72	  devices.
73	- **Any automated or battery-triggered shutdown must detach Longhorn volumes or
74	  stop k3s first.** Without that step it is not a shutdown, it is a delayed
75	  unclean cut. This blocks NUT-driven `ONBATT` automation, not merely delays it.
76	- **ICMP is not a state signal, in either direction.** On the way up it answers
77	  only after the kernel brings up the NIC, well past POST. On the way down it
78	  keeps answering long after sshd is gone. The real tell that teardown is
79	  underway is **sshd refusing while ICMP still answers.**
80	- **Outlet state says only that the relay closed.** It carries no claim about
81	  whether the device downstream is running. The V100 fan needs a physical switch
82	  and does not self-start when its outlet is restored.
83	- Remote power-on for sdf1 is a **solved problem** — do not write or reason from
84	  any "no verified remote power-on path" language. The evidence for each path is
85	  in the `sdf1-power` skill.
86	
87	## Repos
88	
89	Public, under `darthzen`: `nemoclaw-ops-agent` · `agent-build-tools` ·
90	`ash4d.com` · `lab-fleet` · `ollama-code-mcp`
91	
92	**Entire-tracked repos** — the write gate in `infra.md` applies to these, and to
93	any repo where `.entire/settings.json` exists:
94	
95	- `~/Developer/lab-fleet`
96	- `~/Developer/agent-build-tools`
97	
98	Check for `.entire/` before writing into any repo not on this list; the list is
99	a convenience, not the test.
100	
101	## Tracks
102	
103	1. **The lab itself** — single-node k3s on `sdf1`, GPU-scheduled, config-as-code
104	   published to `lab-fleet`. Working dirs: `ash4d-lab/`, `lab-capture/`.
105	2. **NemoClaw ops agent** — the flagship. Autonomous delivery and runtime SRE
106	   agent, k8s-native, on-prem inference, documented autonomy ladder, egress
107	   locked. Working dir: `nemoclaw-ops-agent/`.
108	3. **ash4d.com site and edge portal** — the public site is a Cloudflare Workers
109	   static-assets deployment, published by GitHub Actions from `site/` in
110	   `darthzen/ash4d.com`. No home-lab dependency in its serving path. Plus the

# Ash4d lab conventions — Rick Ashford

Read by any skill that touches the ash4d home lab, the `_portfolio` folder, or
the `darthzen` repos. This file holds the **conventions**, which are stable.
Live state — addresses, chart versions, GPU UUIDs, incident history — belongs
in Claude memory and on the boards, not here.

Companion files: `infra.md` (containers, git, sandbox), `working.md`
(interaction and verification), `skills.md` (authoring and syncing the `sdf1-*`
skills that act on this hardware).

## Identity

- GitHub account is **darthzen**. `rickashford` is the Upwork and LinkedIn
  handle only — never a repo path.

## What the lab is for

`_portfolio` (in Dropbox → Job Search) is the hub. It serves three purposes at
once, and a proposal that helps one at the cost of another needs saying out
loud:

- **Resume proof.** Until there is a catalog of completed contract work, the
  self-built environment *is* the proof — real systems, real repos, real
  security models.
- **Demo platform.** The same services double as customer and portfolio demos.
- **Self-learning lab.** A live cluster to build on, break, and learn from.

## Source of truth

**Running systems and the GitHub boards are authoritative for status. The
markdown docs are design and rationale.**

- A doc that tracks live status links to the board instead of duplicating it.
  This convention exists specifically to stop recurring doc drift.
- Before reconciling or restating any status claim, verify against the board or
  the running system. Status written in a doc is a point-in-time snapshot and
  is assumed stale until checked.
- Never claim work is done that has not been verified done. This is the hard
  rule the whole convention protects.

## Host administration

- Lab hosts are **salt-managed**. Configure them through states in `ash4d-salt`
  rather than by hand, and see *Configuration management* in `infra.md` for the
  rules and the salt/Fleet boundary.
- The salt master is deliberately **outside k3s and outside the power
  authority** — it manages khyron and sdf1, so it cannot live on them, and
  rhubarb stays a simple appliance.

## Cluster dependencies

- **sdf1 does not depend on Rancher.** A managed cluster keeps running whether
  the management cluster is up or not. What needs khyron is changing **Fleet
  state** and the **Rancher admin UI** — never the workloads themselves.
- So Rancher being unreachable is not an sdf1 outage. Do not write a tool, a
  runbook, or a recovery step that treats it as one, and never let a call
  against the `rancher` context block an action on `sdf1`. Bound those calls
  with a timeout and let them fail.

## sdf1 power and shutdown

Durable constraints of the hardware and the storage layer. Current
measurements — recovery times, UPS load, BIOS values — are state and live in
Claude memory and the `sdf1-power` skill, not here.

- **Never plan a time-boxed graceful shutdown of sdf1.** `shutdown -h now` hangs
  on Longhorn iSCSI teardown: k3s stops the Longhorn engine pods early, then
  every later step blocks on devices that can no longer answer. Measured at 21
  minutes with no sign of completing, and it ended in an AC cut. An explicit
  `sync` returning `Dirty: 0` does not help — the final flush syncs *all* block
  devices.
- **Any automated or battery-triggered shutdown must detach Longhorn volumes or
  stop k3s first.** Without that step it is not a shutdown, it is a delayed
  unclean cut. This blocks NUT-driven `ONBATT` automation, not merely delays it.
- **ICMP is not a state signal, in either direction.** On the way up it answers
  only after the kernel brings up the NIC, well past POST. On the way down it
  keeps answering long after sshd is gone. The real tell that teardown is
  underway is **sshd refusing while ICMP still answers.**
- **Outlet state says only that the relay closed.** It carries no claim about
  whether the device downstream is running. The V100 fan needs a physical switch
  and does not self-start when its outlet is restored.
- Remote power-on for sdf1 is a **solved problem** — do not write or reason from
  any "no verified remote power-on path" language. The evidence for each path is
  in the `sdf1-power` skill.

## Repos

Public, under `darthzen`: `nemoclaw-ops-agent` · `agent-build-tools` ·
`ash4d.com` · `lab-fleet` · `ollama-code-mcp`

**Entire-tracked repos** — the write gate in `infra.md` applies to these, and to
any repo where `.entire/settings.json` exists:

- `~/Developer/lab-fleet`
- `~/Developer/agent-build-tools`

Check for `.entire/` before writing into any repo not on this list; the list is
a convenience, not the test.

## Tracks

1. **The lab itself** — single-node k3s on `sdf1`, GPU-scheduled, config-as-code
   published to `lab-fleet`. Working dirs: `ash4d-lab/`, `lab-capture/`.
2. **NemoClaw ops agent** — the flagship. Autonomous delivery and runtime SRE
   agent, k8s-native, on-prem inference, documented autonomy ladder, egress
   locked. Working dir: `nemoclaw-ops-agent/`.
3. **ash4d.com site and edge portal** — the public site is a Cloudflare Workers
   static-assets deployment, published by GitHub Actions from `site/` in
   `darthzen/ash4d.com`. No home-lab dependency in its serving path. Plus the
   browser-anywhere gated demo portal. Working dir: `ash4d-site/`.
   *(The Fleet-managed k3s origin on GCP was retired 2026-08-02 — instance,
   static IP, GitRepo and namespace all deleted.)*
4. **Supporting repos** — the public showcase itself.

## Naming and layout habits

- Numbered component directories (`00–14`) double as recreate order.
- Plan / handoff / tickets split: `PLAN.md` is the locked design, `HANDOFF.md`
  is state and history, `TICKETS-DRAFT.md` is the authoring reference.
- Handoff docs are written to be executed by a different agent in a different
  session — they carry the file list and destination paths, not narrative.

37	  is the interesting part.

39	  blocks until every minion returns and will time out on a real highstate.
40	- Every job is recorded in the master job cache with user, target, function and
41	  arguments. That record is the audit trail. Do not SSH to a host to do
42	  something salt could have done — it bypasses the record.
43	- Minion layout is not uniform. Package names, config paths and service names
44	  differ between stock `salt-minion` and the Uyuni Salt Bundle; branch on the
45	  `saltpath` grain rather than `os_family`. Which host runs which is state —
46	  it lives in Claude memory, not here.
47

52	  command.

64	  does not run those hooks, so anything Cowork writes into the repo lands with
65	  no checkpoint lineage and the repo's provenance breaks silently.
66	- Instead: stage the artifacts to the session scratch dir or the mounted
67	  `_portfolio` folder, then hand me the file list and intended destination
68	  paths so I can run it through Claude Code in one step. If something genuinely
69	  must land immediately — a live incident — say so and get explicit
70	  authorisation first.
71	- Applying manifests to a cluster with `kubectl` is fine. It is repo *files*
72	  that are gated.
73	- Known entire-tracked repos are listed in `lab.md`.

78	  it is missing, stop and tell me — do not commit. Never claim entire.io is
79	  enabled; it can only be verified, not enabled by you.

94	  preferences file, or a repo.
95	- Do not copy a token, key, or PAT into any file you create, including files in
96	  this folder. Reference where it lives instead.
97

101	  them, which strands `index.lock` and blocks every later git command. If a

# The ServiceAccount External Secrets presents to OpenBao. It needs no RBAC of
# its own — OpenBao's Kubernetes auth backend validates the token and maps it
# to a policy. The binding is on OpenBao's side, in the postStart script of
# ../openbao/values.yaml:
#
#   bao write auth/kubernetes/role/openchoreo-secret-writer-role \
#     bound_service_account_names="*" \
#     bound_service_account_namespaces="openbao,openchoreo-workflow-plane"
#
# — which is why this SA must live in the `openbao` namespace specifically.
# Moving it anywhere else silently fails authentication.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: external-secrets-openbao
  namespace: openbao
---
# Cluster-scoped, and named `default` because four other files reference that
# string (see fleet.yaml).
#
# `provider.vault` is correct despite the backend being OpenBao: OpenBao is a
# Vault fork and speaks the same API, and External Secrets has no separate
# provider for it.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      # In-cluster address. OpenBao is deliberately not routable from the
      # gateway — nothing in ../control-plane-extras/ingress.yaml exposes it.
      server: "http://openbao.openbao.svc:8200"
      path: "secret"
      version: "v2"
      auth:
        kubernetes:
          mountPath: "kubernetes"
          role: "openchoreo-secret-writer-role"
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: "external-secrets-openbao"
            namespace: "openbao"
# Observability-plane credentials, pulled from OpenBao through the `default`
# ClusterSecretStore (../secret-store/).

# The observer's OIDC client secret. Named by `observer.secretName` in
# ../observability-plane/values.yaml, whose chart REFUSES TO RENDER without
# it. The key name is fixed by the observer binary — it reads the env var
# UID_RESOLVER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET directly, so `secretKey` here is not free
# to change.
#
# The value must equal the openchoreo-observer-resource-reader-client secret
# in ../thunder/values.yaml.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: observer-secret
  namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: observer-secret
  data:
    - secretKey: UID_RESOLVER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
      remoteRef: { key: observer-oauth-client-secret, property: value }
---
# OpenSearch admin credentials, shared by four consumers:
#   ../observability-logs/    — OpenSearch itself, its setup Job, and fluent-bit
#   ../observability-traces/  — the tracing setup Job and OTel exporter
#   ../observability-events/  — the events OTel collector's basicauth extension
# All four reference this Secret BY NAME, so renaming it means editing all
# four values files.
#
# 🔴 THE PASSWORD IS WRITE-ONCE. OpenSearch seeds its internal security index
# from OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD on FIRST START ONLY
# (../observability-logs/values.yaml). Changing the value in OpenBao later
# rotates what every client presents, but NOT what OpenSearch accepts — the
# result is a cluster nothing can authenticate to. Rotating it properly means
# an OpenSearch-side password change, or deleting its PVC and starting over.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  data:
    - secretKey: username
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-username, property: value }
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-password, property: value }
# Fleet bundle — Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) for ash4d.com.
#
# Replaces the GCP edge VM (35.208.14.166) as the public entry point. Two
# cloudflared replicas hold outbound QUIC connections to Cloudflare; public
# hostnames route through the tunnel to Traefik (or straight to the Ollama
# LoadBalancer VIP, which has no Ingress). No inbound ports are opened.
#
# Tunnel: ash4d-home, a7ac2482-e55f-49ea-a352-0028a54748c3, created
# 2026-08-01 via API (config_src: local — this ConfigMap is authoritative,
# the CF dashboard's ingress editor is not).
#
# MANUAL PREREQUISITE — Secret `cloudflared-credentials` (key
# credentials.json) must exist in this namespace before the Deployment can
# start. Canonical copy: ~/Developer/keys/cloudflare/ash4d-home-tunnel.json
# on Rick's Mac. It is deliberately NOT in OpenBao: openbao-0 runs `server
# -dev` (in-memory), so a pod restart would wipe it and the public site
# would stay down after any power event until someone reseeded it. Revisit
# if OpenBao moves to server mode with persistent storage.
#
# Image is cloudflare/cloudflared, not a BCI wrapper — deviation from the
# SUSE-base default authorized by Rick 2026-08-01: cloudflared is a single
# static Go binary on a vendor-signed release channel, and a BCI wrapper
# adds a build/update path without reducing attack surface.
defaultNamespace: cloudflare-tunnel
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cloudflared
  namespace: cloudflare-tunnel
spec:
  # Single-node cluster, so 2 replicas only cover pod-level restarts (image
  # pulls, OOM, rollouts) — each holds 4 connections to 2 CF data centres.
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cloudflared
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cloudflared
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cloudflared
          image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.7.3
          args: ["tunnel", "--config", "/etc/cloudflared/config/config.yaml", "run"]
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 2000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 10m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/cloudflared/config
              readOnly: true
            - name: creds
              mountPath: /etc/cloudflared/creds
              readOnly: true

content.content:
# tunnel-client Overview

## What It Does

`tunnel-client` is OpenAI's customer-run agent that "connects a private or localhost MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to ChatGPT, Codex, the Responses API, and AgentKit through an OpenAI-hosted MCP tunnel endpoint, while keeping the MCP server off the public internet."

The client operates by:
- Long-polling the OpenAI control plane over HTTPS
- Forwarding JSON-RPC requests to your configured MCP server
- Exposing an admin/health server with `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`
- Running a lightweight admin UI at `/ui` for operational status

## Configuration Methods

The README documents three primary configuration approaches:

**1. Command-line flags** (via `tunnel-client run`):
```
--control-plane.tunnel-id
--control-plane.api-key
--mcp.server-url
--cloudflared.managed
--cloudflared.token
```

**2. Environment variables:**
- `CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID` - tunnel identifier
- `CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY` - runtime API key for authentication
- `CLOUDFLARED_TOKEN` - for Cloudflare tunnel configuration
- `MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_TIMEOUT` - optional startup delay

**3. Configuration files** via profiles:
```
tunnel-client init --sample <profile> --tunnel-id <id>
tunnel-client run --profile-file ./profiles/local-stdio.yaml
```

## Deployment Documentation

Docker, Kubernetes, and VM guidance is available at `docs/deployment/overview.md`. The official releases include "Docker images published at `ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client` for Linux `amd64` and `arm64`" with bundled `cloudflared` companion.

# Kubernetes Deployment Guide Summary

Based on the provided documentation, here are the key elements:

**Deployment Configuration:**
"apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tunnel-client
spec:
  replicas: 5"

**Image Reference:**
The example uses `"image: ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client:v1.2.3"` with a note to replace the version tag with an actual released version or digest.

**Environment Variables:**
- `"CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID"` - set to tunnel identifier
- `"MCP_SERVER_URL"` - points to the MCP server endpoint
- `"HEALTH_LISTEN_ADDR"` - configured as `":8080"`
- `"CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY"` - sourced from a Kubernetes Secret

**Health Monitoring:**
The configuration includes `"livenessProbe"` and `"readinessProbe"` with `"httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: health }"` and `"{ path: /readyz, port: health }"` respectively.

**Architecture Notes:**
The guide emphasizes that multiple replicas work safely only when the MCP server target handles "active-active" traffic, with each message delivered to whichever replica polls first. For non-sticky backends, maintaining one client per tunnel is recommended.

*Note: The documentation doesn't cover Secret/Service manifests, cloudflared modes, or resource requests/limits.*

# Fleet bundle — Karakeep, the lab-memory bookmark/RAG store (Helm).
#
# Chart pinned to 0.32.0, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather
# than upgrades. All the interesting decisions are in values.yaml — read its
# header before touching anything, especially the two Secret notes.
#
# THIS IS THE ONE ADOPTION IN THIS BATCH THAT RESTARTS A POD. The live
# StatefulSet carries OCR_USE_LLM as its FIRST env entry; the chart emits env
# alphabetically, so OCR_USE_LLM renders between NEXTAUTH_URL and
# OLLAMA_BASE_URL. Same variable, same value, different position — which is
# still a pod-template change, so the karakeep StatefulSet rolls once on
# adoption. Nothing is being reconfigured; the live object had simply been
# hand-edited outside Helm. Expect exactly one karakeep pod replacement and no
# change to karakeep-chrome or karakeep-meilesearch.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRETS (both already exist; this bundle does NOT manage them,
# see values.yaml note 1):
#   karakeep              — NEXTAUTH_SECRET
#   karakeep-meilesearch  — MEILI_MASTER_KEY   (note the chart's spelling)
# If either is missing when this path is enabled, karakeep comes up without a
# session secret and Meilisearch rejects every query.
#
# The MCP servers, the ingest CronJob and the karakeep Certificate are raw
# manifests and live in ./raw — separate path, because Fleet allows one chart
# per path.
defaultNamespace: lab-memory
helm:
  releaseName: karakeep
  repo: https://karakeep-app.github.io/helm-charts
  chart: karakeep
  version: "0.32.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

content.content:
# Fleet GitRepo — cloudflare-tunnel namespace.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-cloudflare-tunnel.yaml
#
# One GitRepo per namespace — see gitrepos/README.md.
#
# LOW RISK for the cluster, HIGH STAKES for the public site: two stateless
# cloudflared pods, no PVCs, no inbound ports — but once DNS cuts over, these
# pods ARE the public entry for ash4d.com. Prerequisite: Secret
# `cloudflared-credentials` must be seeded by hand first (see
# 23-cloudflare-tunnel/fleet.yaml for why it is not in OpenBao).
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-cloudflare-tunnel
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval — see lab-ash4d-origin.yaml for the 2026-07-30
  # gitjob dormancy incident that motivates stating it per-repo.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    - 23-cloudflare-tunnel
  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift ON from day one — this bundle was born in git, nothing was
  # adopted, so there is no live hand-tuning to protect. Change the repo, not
  # the cluster. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
  correctDrift:
    enabled: true

# Fleet bundle — OpenAI tunnel-client (github.com/openai/tunnel-client).
#
# Connects a private MCP server to ChatGPT / Codex / the Responses API through
# an OpenAI-hosted tunnel endpoint. The client long-polls the OpenAI control
# plane over outbound HTTPS and forwards JSON-RPC to the MCP server — no
# inbound ports, no cloudflared companion needed (the managed-cloudflared mode
# in the image is for exposing a *local* server; our target is already
# routable).
#
# MCP target: https://mempalace.ash4d.com — the mempalace MCP service, being
# built as of 2026-08-12. The exact path (bare host vs /mcp) is UNVERIFIED
# until that service lands; adjust MCP_SERVER_URL in the Deployment if the
# server mounts its endpoint under a path.
#
# Egress required: api.openai.com:443 (and mempalace.ash4d.com:443).
#
# MANUAL PREREQUISITE — Secret `tunnel-client-credentials` must exist in this
# namespace before the Deployment can start. Canonical copy: 1Password item
# "ChatGPT - Hermes" (Private vault, API_CREDENTIAL). Seed it with:
#
#   kubectl --context sdf1 -n openai-tunnel create secret generic tunnel-client-credentials \
#     --from-literal=CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY="$(op read 'op://Private/ChatGPT - Hermes/credential')" \
#     --from-literal=CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID="$(op read 'op://Private/ChatGPT - Hermes/tunnel id')"
#
# The `tunnel id` field does not exist on the item yet — it is issued when the
# tunnel is created on the OpenAI side, and must be added to the 1Password
# item before seeding. Deliberately NOT in OpenBao for the same reason as
# cloudflared-credentials (23-cloudflare-tunnel/fleet.yaml): openbao-0 runs
# `server -dev` (in-memory), so a pod restart would wipe it.
#
# Image is ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client, not a BCI wrapper — vendor-maintained
# upstream image, used directly per the container policy in infra.md.
defaultNamespace: openai-tunnel

input.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tunnel-client
  namespace: openai-tunnel
spec:
  # ONE replica, deliberately. Upstream docs: multiple replicas are only safe
  # when the MCP backend handles active-active traffic — each message is
  # delivered to whichever replica polls first. mempalace has not been
  # verified active-active, so keep one client per tunnel until it is.
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: tunnel-client
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: tunnel-client
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: tunnel-client
          image: ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client:v0.0.11
          env:
            # Both from the manually seeded Secret — see fleet.yaml header.
            - name: CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: tunnel-client-credentials
                  key: CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID
            - name: CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: tunnel-client-credentials
                  key: CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY
            # Path unverified until the mempalace MCP service lands — see
            # fleet.yaml header before "fixing" anything here.
            - name: MCP_SERVER_URL
              value: "https://mempalace.ash4d.com"
            - name: HEALTH_LISTEN_ADDR
              value: ":8080"
          ports:
            - name: health
              containerPort: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: health
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: health
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 10m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi

# Fleet GitRepo — openai-tunnel namespace.
#
# Points Fleet at 24-openai-tunnel (OpenAI tunnel-client → mempalace MCP).
# Lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`):
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openai-tunnel.yaml
#
# One GitRepo per namespace — see gitrepos/README.md.
#
# LOW RISK: one stateless pod, no PVCs, no inbound ports. Prerequisite:
# Secret `tunnel-client-credentials` must be seeded by hand first (see
# 24-openai-tunnel/fleet.yaml for the op:// seed command and why it is not
# in OpenBao).
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-openai-tunnel
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval — see lab-ash4d-origin.yaml for the 2026-07-30
  # gitjob dormancy incident that motivates stating it per-repo.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    - 24-openai-tunnel
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift ON from day one — born in git, nothing adopted.
  correctDrift:
    enabled: true

input.description:
Bundle 24-openai-tunnel is written and validated in lab-fleet (iCloud copy), uncommitted. Files: 24-openai-tunnel/fleet.yaml, 24-openai-tunnel/tunnel-client.deployment.yaml, 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openai-tunnel.yaml.

STEPS
1. Create the tunnel on the OpenAI side (platform tunnel endpoint for ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client) — this issues the tunnel ID. Docs: https://github.com/openai/tunnel-client
2. Add a field named exactly "tunnel id" to the 1Password item "ChatGPT - Hermes" (Private vault) holding that ID. The API key is already in the item's "credential" field.
3. Review + commit + push the three files (main, darthzen/lab-fleet).
4. Seed the secret:
kubectl --context sdf1 create namespace openai-tunnel
kubectl --context sdf1 -n openai-tunnel create secret generic tunnel-client-credentials \
  --from-literal=CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY="$(op read 'op://Private/ChatGPT - Hermes/credential')" \
  --from-literal=CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID="$(op read 'op://Private/ChatGPT - Hermes/tunnel id')"
5. Register the bundle:
kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openai-tunnel.yaml
6. Verify: pod Ready in openai-tunnel ns (readyz gates on control-plane connection). MCP_SERVER_URL is set to https://mempalace.ash4d.com — confirm the path once the mempalace MCP service is live; adjust in the Deployment if it mounts under /mcp.

Steps 4–6 can be handed to Claude Code once 1–3 are done.

content.text:
The bundle is written and validated, uncommitted per your git rule, with a 9:15 block tomorrow for the parts only you can do.

**Files created** (iCloud copy of lab-fleet, both copies are entire-tracked clones):
- `24-openai-tunnel/fleet.yaml` — bundle header documents the manual Secret prerequisite with the `op://` seed command, and why it stays out of OpenBao (same dev-mode wipe risk as cloudflared-credentials)
- `24-openai-tunnel/tunnel-client.deployment.yaml` — `ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client:v0.0.11`, 1 replica (upstream says multi-replica is only safe against an active-active MCP backend, and mempalace isn't verified for that), key and tunnel ID from Secret `tunnel-client-credentials`, `MCP_SERVER_URL=https://mempalace.ash4d.com`, health probes on :8080
- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openai-tunnel.yaml` — mirrors the cloudflare-tunnel GitRepo pattern; passed a server dry-run against the Rancher controller (dry-run only, nothing applied)

**Verified along the way:**
- No 1Password plugin is installed in Claude Code — what worked is the `op` CLI with your desktop-app integration, which authorized when I called it. Good enough; no plugin needed.
- The API key is 1Password item **"ChatGPT - Hermes"** (Private vault), `credential` field, `sk-…` ×164 chars. I read field metadata only, never the value.

**Assumptions, flagged:**
- `MCP_SERVER_URL` is the bare host `https://mempalace.ash4d.com` — the real path is unknowable until the mempalace MCP service lands. Noted in both manifests.
- The Secret expects a `tunnel id` field on the 1Password item that doesn't exist yet — the ID is issued when you create the tunnel on the OpenAI side.

**Blocked on you** (calendar event tomorrow 9:15–9:45 CT, between the FOSSA follow-up and the Logic block, full commands embedded): create the tunnel at OpenAI, add the `tunnel id` field to the 1Password item, commit and push. Once those are done I can seed the Secret and apply the GitRepo from here — say go.

Not yet — the endpoint doesn't exist, though the plumbing in front of it does.

- **`mempalace.ash4d.com`**: DNS resolves (192.168.7.150, the internal Traefik VIP) and TLS answers, but both `/` and `/mcp` return **404** — no Ingress routes that hostname yet. The MCP service isn't deployed, which matches "being built right now."
- **My session-local mempalace MCP**: fully working — 72,938 drawers, and notably it's now running on the **Milvus backend**, so the palace data is already served out of the cluster's Milvus (bundle 06). The 404 hostname is presumably the network path to that same store once its MCP server lands.

One implication for the tunnel bundle, flagged as inference: since 192.168.7.150 is answering for the hostname already, the tunnel-client pod will reach it in-cluster as soon as the Ingress appears — no change needed to `MCP_SERVER_URL`, only the path question remains (bare host vs `/mcp`) once the service is live.

It's live now — and it wants auth.

- `/mcp` moved from **404 → 401 Unauthorized** since the last probe: the service landed behind Traefik in the last few minutes and answers with an authorization challenge (the error page is Python `http.server` style, so it's the mempalace server itself responding, not Traefik).
- `/` is still 404, which is fine — the MCP surface is mounted at **`/mcp`**, so the Deployment's `MCP_SERVER_URL` should become `https://mempalace.ash4d.com/mcp`. I'll make that edit on your word.

What I can't do is authenticate: I don't know what token or scheme it expects, and the only candidate I've seen — the `ChatGPT - Hermes` credential — is the OpenAI control-plane key, which shouldn't double as the MCP server's own auth. Two things to settle:

1. What auth does the mempalace MCP expect (header and where the token lives)?
2. The tunnel-client will need to present that same auth when forwarding — the docs mention OAuth/mTLS handling, so there's likely a `--mcp.*` auth flag; I'll dig that out of the docs once you tell me the scheme.

content.content:
# MCP Server Authentication & Header Options

## Bearer Tokens & Custom Headers

**Static MCP Headers:**
- Flag: `--mcp.extra-headers "Key: Value"` (repeatable)
- Environment: `MCP_EXTRA_HEADERS="Key: Value, Key2: Value2"`
- YAML: `mcp.extra_headers`

Description: "Header values accept `env:VARNAME` and `file:/path/to/secret`; all other values are treated literally."

Scope: "sent only to the configured MCP server origin for outbound MCP HTTP traffic. These headers are not sent to the OpenAI control plane or unrelated authorization-server hosts."

Conflict behavior: "connector-forwarded request headers are applied last and override these static values case-insensitively."

**Discovery/Probe Headers:**
- Flag: `--mcp.discovery-extra-headers "Key: Value"` (repeatable)
- Environment: `MCP_DISCOVERY_EXTRA_HEADERS="Key: Value, Key2: Value2"`
- YAML: `mcp.discovery_extra_headers`

Scope: "sent only to MCP discovery/probe requests for the configured MCP server origin, including OAuth Protected Resource Metadata discovery."

## mTLS Client Certificates

**Defaults (all HTTP channels):**
- `--mcp.client-cert=<path|env:VAR>` / `MCP_CLIENT_CERT`
- `--mcp.client-key=<path|env:VAR>` / `MCP_CLIENT_KEY`

**Per-channel overrides** in server-url:
```
--mcp.server-url="channel=analytics,url=https://...,client-cert=/path,client-key=/path"
```

## YAML Profile Example

```yaml
mcp:
  server_urls:
    - channel: main
      url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
  extra_headers:
    X-Internal-Auth: env:MCP_RUNTIME_HEADER_VALUE
  discovery_extra_headers:
    X-Discovery-Auth: file:/run/secrets/mcp-discovery-header
```

  name: tunnel-client
  namespace: openai-tunnel

  # ONE replica, deliberately. Upstream docs: multiple replicas are only safe
  # when the MCP backend handles active-active traffic — each message is
  # delivered to whichever replica polls first. mempalace has not been
  # verified active-active, so keep one client per tunnel until it is.
  replicas: 1
  selector:

    spec:
      containers:
        - name: tunnel-client
          image: ghcr.io/openai/tunnel-client:v0.0.11
          env:

            - name: CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID

content.text:
The mempalace token is wired into the bundle and everything re-validates.

- **Auth confirmed working**: `op://Private/Lab Memory/mempalace-mcp-token` as `Authorization: Bearer` gets HTTP 200 from `https://mempalace.ash4d.com/mcp` — server `mempalace` v3.6.0, 22 read-only tools listed.
- **Deployment updated**: `MCP_SERVER_URL` now `…/mcp`; the token flows Secret → `MEMPALACE_MCP_TOKEN` env → Kubernetes `$(VAR)` expansion into `MCP_AUTH_HEADER` → tunnel-client's `MCP_EXTRA_HEADERS` with its `env:` substitution. Per the docs, `MCP_EXTRA_HEADERS` is sent only to the MCP origin, never to the OpenAI control plane. One caveat worth knowing: connector-forwarded request headers override these statics case-insensitively, so if ChatGPT ever forwards its own `Authorization` header it would win — something to watch at end-to-end test time, flagged as a docs-derived behavior I haven't observed.
- **fleet.yaml** header and the **9:15 calendar block** both carry the updated three-line seed command including `MEMPALACE_MCP_TOKEN`.
- Client dry-run passes on the Deployment; YAML parses clean. Files remain uncommitted.

Still blocked on the same two items only you can do: the tunnel ID from the OpenAI side (then add the `tunnel id` field to `ChatGPT - Hermes`), and the commit/push. After that I can seed and apply on a "go."

content.text:
Everything except the commit is done.

- **1Password**: `tunnel id` field added to `ChatGPT - Hermes` with `tunnel_6a7cd3bedb408191ae74a75de3f0f66d`. One incident to know about: my `op item edit` silently renamed the item to `ChatGPT` as a side effect — cause unverified, likely an op CLI quirk with the field-assignment syntax. I caught it on read-back and restored the title; credential and username fields were untouched throughout.
- **Secret**: `tunnel-client-credentials` created in the new `openai-tunnel` namespace on sdf1, verified by decoding key lengths — API key 164B, tunnel ID 39B, mempalace token 43B, no trailing newlines.
- **Calendar block** (tomorrow 9:15) updated to reflect the done state.

The one remaining blocker is yours: review, commit, and push the three files on `main`. The moment they're on origin, say go and I'll apply the GitRepo to the Rancher controller and watch the pod come Ready — `readyz` gates on the control-plane connection, so a Ready pod means the tunnel is actually established, and then an end-to-end tool call from the ChatGPT side proves the whole path.

# Fleet bundle — OpenAI tunnel-client (github.com/openai/tunnel-client).
#
# Connects a private MCP server to ChatGPT / Codex / the Responses API through
# an OpenAI-hosted tunnel endpoint. The client long-polls the OpenAI control
# plane over outbound HTTPS and forwards JSON-RPC to the MCP server — no
# inbound ports, no cloudflared companion needed (the managed-cloudflared mode
# in the image is for exposing a *local* server; our target is already
# routable).
#
# MCP target: https://mempalace.ash4d.com/mcp — the mempalace MCP server
# (v3.6.0, 22 read-only tools). Verified live 2026-08-12: Streamable HTTP at
# /mcp, Bearer auth, no session header. The hostname resolves to the internal
# Traefik VIP (192.168.7.150), so the tunnel-client pod reaches it in-cluster.
#
# Egress required: api.openai.com:443 (and mempalace.ash4d.com:443).
#
# MANUAL PREREQUISITE — Secret `tunnel-client-credentials` must exist in this
# namespace before the Deployment can start. Canonical copy: 1Password item
# "ChatGPT - Hermes" (Private vault, API_CREDENTIAL). Seed it with:
#
#   kubectl --context sdf1 -n openai-tunnel create secret generic tunnel-client-credentials \

#     --from-literal=CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID="$(op read 'op://Private/ChatGPT - Hermes/tunnel id')" \
#     --from-literal=MEMPALACE_MCP_TOKEN="$(op read 'op://Private/Lab Memory/mempalace-mcp-token')"
#
# The mempalace token (item "Lab Memory", Private vault) is the Bearer token
# the client presents to the MCP server via MCP_EXTRA_HEADERS.
# The `tunnel id` field does not exist on the item yet — it is issued when the
# tunnel is created on the OpenAI side, and must be added to the 1Password
# item before seeding. Deliberately NOT in OpenBao for the same reason as

---
name: 1password-item-standard
description: Rick's 1Password layout — one item per service, one concealed field per consumer
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

1Password items are named for the **service** (e.g. `ChatGPT`, `Buzz`, `Claude`, `Lab Memory`, all in the Private vault), with one CONCEALED field per consumer/key (e.g. `hermes-lab` on ChatGPT; `mempalace-mcp-token` on Lab Memory; per-agent fields like `alice`, `zaphod` on Buzz). The built-in `credential` field may stay populated but the named field is the reference to use: `op read 'op://Private/<Service>/<consumer>'`.

**Why:** service-named items with per-consumer fields keep one item per vendor and make `op://` references self-describing.

**How to apply:** when storing a new key, add a concealed field to the existing service item rather than creating a `<Service> - <consumer>` item. Beware: `op item edit <uuid> "field[type]=value"` once silently truncated the item title (`ChatGPT - Hermes` → `ChatGPT`); verify the title after any edit.
